Durability analysis of CNT embedded GLARE structure through matrix and Al surface modification strategies

Abstract:

This study focuses on the modification of glass fiber laminate aluminum reinforced epoxy (GLARE) laminates using functionalized carbon nanotube (F-CNTs). Surface treated aluminum sheets along with glass fabric and epoxy resin modified with carboxyl functionalized carbon nanotubes (F-CNT) of different concentration (0, 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5) were used to fabricate the laminates through vacuum bagging. Based on the drop shape analysis, 0.3 wt% F-CNT embedded epoxy showed best wettability with both glass fiber and aluminum sheet. Key mechanical tests, such as flexural, short beam shear and interlaminar fracture toughness (ILFT) under mode &ndash I and II loadings were performed to assess the mechanical performance of fabricated GLAREs. Among all the laminates, 0.3wt% F-CNT embedded GLARE shows maximum delamination resistance, as observed in its interlaminar shear strength, which is ~19% higher over the neat laminate. The same laminate exhibited improved damage tolerance, in terms of critical energy release rate under mode I and II ILFT loadings, which were found to be ~23% and ~14% better over the neat laminate respectively. The storage modulus (E&rsquo) 0.3 wt.% F-CNT reinforcement laminates exhibit ~13% higher than neat laminates. These improvements across various tests may be attributed to the homogeneous dispersion of F-CNTs within the matrix, improved interfacial adhesion between (a) glass fiber and modified epoxy and (b) aluminum sheets and glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) layers, as observed from fractographic analysis done using scanning electron microscopy.
